expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: export type Subscription = | TrialingSubscription | ActiveSubscription | PastDueSubscription | CanceledSubscription; with readonly status: 'trialing' etc. on each variant

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: CanceledSubscription has only status, canceledAt, cancellation; TrialingSubscription has only status, trialEndsAt — no field overlap

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: export function assertNever(value: never): never... with default: return assertNever(sub) in hasProductAccess switch

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: type Brand<T, B extends string> = T & { readonly [brand]: B }; export type SubscriptionId = Brand<string, 'SubscriptionId'>; CustomerId, PlanId also branded

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: Provides checkTransition(from, to) function structure; discriminated union constrains what fields exist on each state

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Names multiple misuses prevented: 'without that default, adding paused next year compiles clean and silently denies access everywhere'; 'unbounded one lets a bug charge a dead card forever' (prevents via bounded RetryCount); prevents {voluntary: true, reason: 'payment_failed'} via nested union

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Explicitly contrasts with flat interface and explains 128 illegal combinations exist in bag-of-optionals; recommends and implements discriminated union instead
